scope: New manual-only reboot entry; compare direct digital reset, prearmed RTC fallback and direct wrapped noos. No production/SDK edits, IDF build or hardware by reviewer.
actual_host_result: 74 actual USB owner/descriptors scenarios passed across vendor and CDC; synthetic registers/RTOS/reset stubs, not physical reset/DMA proof.
baseline_ELF_note: Recorded ELF c47a3710a770506abd030d03790b58c137150c9c1cba86a596f07962114a3c4e predates the new manual entry. It proves the pinned unchanged SDK/wrapper structure only; the new manual call target still needs final-image disassembly.

decision.selected: sensorarrayUsbOtgManualRestart(romDownload): only explicitly accepted manual RESTART/USBBOOT, same absolute250000us USB preparation; on success call esp_restart_noos through existing --wrap; on failure retain original EmergencyCoreReset branch. Main PerformManualRestart is the sole production caller.
decision.why_all_manual: Conditioning only on observed Wi-Fi quarantine misses a newly stuck esp_wifi_stop shutdown callback and the observer sampling window. The dedicated manual entry removes the known shutdown-handler dependency for every accepted manual escape; generic/AUTO paths remain unchanged.
decision.acceptance_boundary: Existing RACK local-publish barrier and cached RAPP restarting intent remain. Twenty-millisecond publication opportunity is not PC receipt. The manual function does not perform frontend SAFE transitions or assert physical isolation; it is an explicit terminal reset, not worker/DMA cancellation.

alternatives.option: Reuse EmergencyCoreReset directly after successful Prepare
alternatives.assessment: Digital Core Reset avoids SDK cleanup and resets more peripherals, but current helper unconditionally sets the RTC USB recovery magic. Calling it after successful USBBOOT would undo the intentional release marker. A new latch-preserving variant would need separate review/HIL and does not inherit the existing noos early RTC-watchdog sequence. Not selected.

alternatives.option: Prearm independent RTC hardware watchdog then call esp_restart
alternatives.assessment: Can cover the shutdown-handler wait without a new task/timer, but adds application WDT ownership, clock/eFuse timing, enable/readback and boot/ROM latch handling; noos later reinitializes the watchdog. More code and validation than the selected pinned SDK terminal path. No new WDT policy implemented.

alternatives.option: Prepared manual escape directly to wrapped noos
alternatives.assessment: Smallest selected software change. Existing USB fence and failure recovery remain; normal handler list is bypassed only for accepted manual requests. Actual S3 noos arms RTC fallback before its subsequent teardown. Deliberate private-API use is documented and pinned to exact S3/IDF behavior.

shutdown_handler_audit.project: No esp_register_shutdown_handler call found in main/core/components/managed_components. Current target map links registration references only from Wi-Fi defaults and system-time implementation; do not reuse the ESP32-target BT handler claim for this S3 image.
shutdown_handler_audit.wifi: Default AP handler registration adds esp_wifi_stop. This synchronous handler is the known unbounded pre-noos dependency being bypassed.
shutdown_handler_audit.time: Both RTC and esp_timer time functions are configured; esp_sync_timekeeping_timers updates wall-clock/RTC offset. Skipping its final synchronization can affect gettimeofday continuity. The project has no gettimeofday/settimeofday/time/localtime/gmtime/SNTP calls and scientific frames use boot-scoped esp_timer timestamps; no cross-boot sequence/time ordering is promised.
shutdown_handler_audit.scientific_persistence: Calibration SAVE runs nvs_set_blob, nvs_commit and nvs_close synchronously in the same acquisition command path. Manual reset handling runs at the boundary before subsequent commands, or in init-failed/no-scan control loops. There is no scientific save/SAFE shutdown handler being skipped. This is not a claim that arbitrary SDK NVS activity is globally quiesced; prior generic shutdown was not a global NVS commit barrier either.

actual_noos_order_and_placement.order: At entry disable current-core interrupts; initialize ROM RWDT HAL; compute timeout from RTC slow selector; configure stage0 RESET_SYSTEM and stage1 RESET_RTC; enable flashboot watchdog mode and write protection; only then TG watchdog terminal handling, external-stack check, other-core reset/stall, cache disable, peripheral/UART/clock teardown and CPU reset.
actual_noos_order_and_placement.linked_addresses: Baseline: __wrap_esp_restart_noos0x40377408 and esp_restart_noos0x40384b30 in .iram0.text; rtc_clk_slow_freq_get_hz0x40382214 IRAM. WDT HAL symbols resolve to ROM0x40000dxx/0x40000exx. USB ownership flag is DRAM; recovery pair RTC_NOINIT.
actual_noos_order_and_placement.manual_entry_constraint: Call from the existing task context while cache is usable and with existing internal main/acquisition stacks. The SDK function contains pre-cache-disable constant reads; do not generalize this reviewed entry as an arbitrary cache-off API. Do not add scheduler-lock waits. Private header explicitly warns against ordinary FreeRTOS application use; this is a pinned terminal escape with no return, not a general API recommendation.
actual_noos_order_and_placement.watchdog_limits: Current RTC source is internal RC, SDK approximate136000Hz. rtc_clk_slow_freq_get_hz reads selector and returns a constant, without calibration waits. SDK comments nominal1s; TRM stage0 depends on EFUSE_WDT_DELAY_SEL and actual oscillator rate, so no exact physical millisecond deadline is established here. Stage0 action resets digital core excluding RTC; stage1 additionally resets RTC, so download/latch retention after fallback is not presumed.
actual_noos_order_and_placement.TRM: Local ESP32-S3 TRM v1.7 sections7.1.3/7.1.4 and13.2.2.1-.4: CPU/Core/System reset levels, RTC slow-clock watchdog, stage0 eFuse factor and flashboot mode.

latch_and_ownership_review: PrepareRestart success is required before the new direct noos branch. Existing USB owner disables IRQ, detaches with20ms engineering dwell, resets module and reads reset bit before clearing hardwareMayOwnDma and publishing quiesced.
Successful USBBOOT retains verified force-download flag and cleared recovery magic. New manual entry does not rewrite the magic; existing wrapper sees DMA guard clear and forwards to real noos.
Failed/late Prepare retains original emergency branch: no new ROM arm, persistent buffers not reclaimed, recovery magic forces USJ fallback. Existing boot latch is not consumed by ordinary restart.
Unknown SDK/DMA completion is not changed into verified cleanup. Reset is terminal hardware action; no task deletion, socket close, slot freeing or reuse is introduced by this increment.
required_final_target_checks: Build exact candidate and record ELF/source hashes. Disassemble sensorarrayUsbOtgManualRestart: success call must resolve to __wrap_esp_restart_noos, not bypass guard or call esp_restart; generic sensorarrayUsbOtgRestart remains esp_restart.

Confirm wrapper guard is DRAM and its emergency branch plus real noos reachable text/literals are IRAM/ROM where required; RTC recovery magic remains RTC_NOINIT. New manual entry may be flash because it executes before cache disable.
Confirm final image noos still arms RWDT before subsequent teardown and HAL symbols/SDK version have not changed; no new background task/timer/watchdog-disabling policy was added.
Inspect all call sites: only accepted manual PerformManualRestart uses new API; automatic recovery/SDK callers retain existing route.
required_safe_HIL_not_run: Manual application RESTART with normal USB reads: capture accepted request/terminal as available, USB detach/reappearance, fresh BUILD/boot/session/READY, no BOOT button action. Report actual reset latency separately from host enumeration latency.

Explicit USBBOOT from healthy OTG and from existing USJ recovery: verify ROM enumeration/chip identity and a recoverable authorized return to application without BOOT manipulation. No whole-chip erase or CAL SAVE.
AP-active/AP-failed/quarantined manual reset on the final Wi-Fi candidate as safely available; document hardware fault-injection limits. Host stubs alone do not prove a live blocked SDK recovery.
USB owner no-ACK/late-ACK remains host-injected unless separately authorized hardware conditions exist; observe USJ recovery before claiming escape from unknown DMA.
After each tested reboot verify scientific startup/identity and controls; do not claim hardware analog SAFE from GPIO/reset state or universal recovery from power/clock faults.
remaining: Target call-target verification and physical boot/USB enumeration acceptance remain mandatory. This closes the reviewed software shutdown-handler dependency only after candidate build/link gate; it does not prove all project P0/P1 or physical recovery.
